assessments: Weekly problem sets, programming exercises, 2 midterms, and 1 final exam.
workload: Challenging course with regular assignments. Requires strong mathematical and problem-solving skills.
advice: Practice algorithms regularly and understand the concepts instead of memorizing solutions.

assessments: Weekly coding exercises, written problem sets, midterm examinations, and a final exam.
workload: Moderately heavy workload. Some assignments are time-consuming, especially graph algorithms and dynamic programming.
advice: Start problem sets early and practice solving problems without looking at solutions.

assessments: Programming assignments, theoretical problem sets, 2 midterms, and a comprehensive final exam.
workload: Heavy workload because the theoretical material can be difficult to understand without consistent practice.
advice: Make sure you understand time complexity, recursion, and dynamic programming before exams.

assessments: SQL assignments, 2 programming projects, quizzes, and a final exam.
workload: Moderate workload. Projects can take time, especially when working with database implementation.
advice: Review SQL and database concepts before the course. Start projects early.

assessments: SQL homework, database design assignments, group project, quizzes, and a final exam.
workload: Fairly manageable if you have previous programming experience. The project requires some additional time.
advice: Practice SQL queries and understand database normalization. Collaborate with classmates when working on projects.

assessments: Programming assignments, database implementation project, quizzes, and a final examination.
workload: Moderately demanding, especially when multiple assignments and project deadlines overlap.
advice: Do not underestimate the projects. Review indexing, transactions, and query optimization.

assessments: Python homework assignments, paper reviews, group research project, project presentations, and final report.
workload: Moderately demanding. Programming assignments and research papers require consistent effort.
advice: Have a good understanding of Python and machine learning fundamentals. Start the final project early.

assessments: Python programming assignments, research paper discussions, paper reviews, and a group project.
workload: Manageable workload if you have prior machine learning experience. Reading research papers takes some extra time.
advice: Stay updated with NLP research and review Python libraries used for text processing.

assessments: Programming assignments, weekly paper readings, individual research project, and final project presentations.
workload: Heavy workload due to the combination of programming, research, and project implementation.
advice: Make sure you understand neural networks and language models. Do not leave paper reviews until the last minute.

assessments: In-class quizzes, programming assignment, midterm, and a course project with a final report and presentation. No final exam.
workload: Quite demanding because of the mathematical concepts and programming requirements. The project requires consistent effort.
advice: Review linear algebra, probability, and Python before taking this course.

assessments: Programming assignment, in-class quizzes, midterm examination, and a customizable final project.
workload: Moderately heavy workload. Training models and completing programming assignments can take considerable time.
advice: Experiment with different neural network architectures and make sure you understand the mathematical foundations.

assessments: Programming assignment, dynamic in-class quizzes, midterm, and a major course project.
workload: Very demanding course, particularly for students without previous machine learning experience.
advice: Review calculus, linear algebra, and probability. Keep up with lectures and start the project early.

assessments: Homework assignments, research paper presentations, midterm examination, group project, and peer review.
workload: Moderately difficult. Requires programming, machine learning knowledge, and an understanding of robotics concepts.
advice: Review machine learning and robotics fundamentals. Keep up with research papers and start the project early.

assessments: Homework assignments, research paper discussions, project proposal, milestone report, and final project presentation.
workload: Interesting but moderately demanding. The research readings and project require consistent effort.
advice: Participate in paper discussions and understand reinforcement learning concepts before working on the project.

assessments: Programming homework, midterm exam, research paper presentations, group project, and individual peer review.
workload: Heavy workload because of the combination of theoretical material, research, and practical project work.
advice: Make sure you have basic machine learning knowledge and divide project responsibilities among teammates.

assessments: Class participation, quizzes, mathematical assignments, a team project presentation, and an individual term report.
workload: Mathematically challenging. Requires understanding of encryption, security protocols, number theory, and probability.
advice: Review modular arithmetic and basic cryptography concepts before starting.

assessments: Quizzes, theoretical problem assignments, mathematical presentations, and a group cryptography project.
workload: Moderately demanding. The theoretical concepts can be difficult, but consistent practice makes them easier to understand.
advice: Focus on understanding encryption algorithms, hashing, and digital signatures. Practice mathematical problems regularly.

assessments: Mathematical assignments, quizzes, research-related presentations, team project, and individual final report.
workload: Heavy workload because of the mathematical foundations and detailed security concepts covered throughout the course.
advice: Do not memorize cryptographic algorithms without understanding how they work. Review number theory and modular arithmetic.

assessments: Game development milestones, collaborative game project, progress reviews, and final game presentation. No traditional exams.
workload: Project-heavy course. Most of the workload comes from developing, testing, and improving the game.
advice: Choose a realistic game idea, divide responsibilities among teammates, and complete a working prototype early.

assessments: Development milestones, weekly progress updates, peer evaluations, team project reviews, and final game demonstration.
workload: Moderately heavy workload. Team coordination and debugging can take more time than expected.
advice: Use version control, communicate regularly with your teammates, and avoid adding too many features close to the deadline.

assessments: Game development assignments, collaborative game project, milestone demonstrations, and final presentation. No traditional exams.
workload: Fairly manageable if you have previous game development experience. The project requires consistent teamwork.
advice: Choose a game engine you are comfortable using and divide the project into smaller tasks. Focus on completing the core gameplay first.
